title: Enterprise hot routes inventory + traffic shapes (MVP input)
content:
Doc purpose
- Working inventory of "hot" API routes + the enterprise tenants that dominate those routes.
- Intended as input to: (a) which routes qualify as Protected Routes in MVP, (b) tier-by-route budgets, (c) routing/admission-control thresholds, (d) SLO dashboard splits.

Definitions (working)
- Protected Route (MVP): A route where (i) enterprise revenue concentration is high, (ii) overload creates cross-fleet impact, and (iii) we have explicit latency/availability commitments.
- Tenant: Redwood account / org. Names below are customer-facing where already common internally; otherwise anonymized.
- Workload shape: request rate + token/seq length distribution + concurrency/streaming characteristics.

Methodology / data sources (rough)
- 14-day window ending 2026-01-19; focus on weekdays 15:00–02:00 UTC (peak overlap US/EU).
- Gateway logs aggregated by route_group + tier + region; approximate token counts from request metadata.
- Runtime: scheduler lag + queue depth snapshots for bursts (where available).
- Caveat: values below are directional; final budgets should use Logan/Nadia’s canonical dashboards once the new metric standards land.

Columns
- Prot? = should be in protected routes allowlist for MVP.
- Enterprise SLO target = goal for enterprise tier on that route in steady state and during best-effort shedding.
- Pain points = what currently causes p95/p99 blow-ups or 5xx under pressure.

Inventory table (top enterprise-weighted routes)
| Route group | Endpoint | Prot? | Primary request type | Default model(s) (current) | Regions (top) | Top tenants (enterprise-weighted) | Avg RPS (enterprise) | Peak 1-min RPS (enterprise) | Burst pattern | Prompt/ctx length distribution (p50/p95, tokens in) | Output distribution (p50/p95, tokens out) | Streaming % | Concurrency notes | Current SLO pain points / observed failure modes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| chat_completions | /v1/chat/completions | Y | chat + tool calling | redwood-chat-large-v3, redwood-chat-medium-v5 (fallback candidate) | us-east, eu-west | Proxima Bank; Acme AI (pilot); Tenant E-014; Tenant E-022 | 110 | 420 | Daily bursts at :00 + :30 (batch job fan-out) + incident-driven retry storms | 680 / 3,200 (long-tail up to 12k for a few tenants) | 180 / 900 | 72% | High concurrent streams; sensitive to head-of-line blocking on long prompts | p99 latency spikes during mixed long/short prompts; occasional 499/stream disconnects during shedding; retry storms amplify queue depth; uneven batching efficiency across ctx lengths |
| embeddings | /v1/embeddings | Y | embeddings (sync) | redwood-embed-v2 | us-east, us-west, eu-west | Acme AI; Tenant E-003; Tenant E-031 | 240 | 980 | Sharp bursts during indexing jobs (10–20 min) | 220 / 1,100 | n/a | 0% | Very high fan-out; many small requests; batch-friendly but punishes gateway if per-request policy eval is heavy | Tail latency increases when queue depth grows; gateway CPU overhead visible at peaks; best-effort traffic currently competes too late (no early admission control) |
| rerank | /v1/rerank | Y | rerank | redwood-rerank-v1 | us-east, eu-west | Tenant E-014; Tenant E-019; Proxima Bank | 60 | 260 | Spiky (search traffic + customer-side timeouts cause retries) | 350 / 1,600 | 1 / 1 (scores only) | 0% | Bursty concurrency; latency-sensitive (user-facing search) | p95 regresses disproportionately when co-scheduled with long-context chat; intermittent 5xx when upstream timeouts cascade |
| responses | /v1/responses | N (later) | unified responses | redwood-chat-large-v3 | us-east | Tenant E-055; Tenant E-022 | 15 | 80 | Moderate; mostly interactive | 900 / 2,800 | 220 / 800 | 64% | Similar to chat, but lower volume today; may become hot as SDK adoption increases | Currently stable; risk is growth-driven; treat as alias to chat group once volume crosses threshold |
| chat_completions_json | /v1/chat/completions (structured) | Y | chat + JSON schema | redwood-chat-large-v3 | us-east | Proxima Bank; Tenant E-022 | 28 | 140 | Bursts correlated with nightly ETL + schema-validation retries | 1,100 / 4,000 | 120 / 500 | 58% | Higher CPU per request due to validation/formatting; smaller outputs but higher failure sensitivity | Elevated 4xx/429 confusion today (quota vs overload indistinguishable); schema retries cause self-amplification under pressure |
| audio_transcribe | /v1/audio/transcriptions | N | ASR | redwood-asr-v1 | us-east | Tenant E-061 | 8 | 30 | Low, periodic | n/a | n/a | 0% | Separate pool in some regions; not a primary fleet risk today | Not in MVP; monitor but avoid adding complexity |
| batch_chat | /v1/batches (chat payloads) | Y (guardrails) | offline batch | redwood-chat-medium-v5 | us-east, eu-west | Tenant E-003; Tenant E-031 | 12 | 55 | Large discrete submissions; can cause sustained pressure for 30–90 min | 750 / 6,000 | 200 / 1,200 | 0% | Sustained queue occupancy; interacts badly with interactive SLOs if not isolated | Primary risk is sustained saturation + starvation of interactive; needs strict admission control + clear scheduling budgets |
| completions_legacy | /v1/completions | N (deprecating) | text completion | redwood-text-v2 | us-east | Tenant E-009 | 5 | 20 | Flat | 500 / 1,200 | 160 / 700 | 0% | Low traffic; legacy clients | Not a top driver; include only if routing config migration requires it |

Top-tenant notes (qualitative)
- Proxima Bank
  - Mix: chat_completions (streaming) + rerank. Very latency-sensitive, user-facing flows.
  - Typical behavior: conservative retries w/ exponential backoff (good citizen), but long-context prompts (2–8k) increase variance.
  - Ask: wants predictable behavior + clear reason codes; open to strict admission control over silent fallback.
- Acme AI (pilot / late-stage prospect)
  - Mix: embeddings (indexing) + chat bursts during eval runs.
  - Typical behavior: very high fan-out indexing jobs; will saturate any shared best-effort pool if not tiered.
  - Ask: explicit enterprise priority + documented quota/burst limits; wants confidence against noisy neighbors.
- Tenant E-014
  - Mix: rerank heavy; spiky traffic (search).
  - Observed: retries triggered by p95 > 900ms; can become self-reinforcing during regional pressure.

Traffic shape summaries (for policy defaults)
- chat_completions
  - Two distinct modes: (1) interactive streaming, (2) long-context analysis jobs disguised as interactive.
  - Recommendation: split route group internally by ctx bucket (e.g., <=2k, 2–8k, >8k) for admission decisions (but keep customer-facing semantics consistent).
- embeddings
  - Batch-friendly; gateway/policy overhead must be low. A few tenants create large synchronized bursts.
  - Recommendation: aggressive early throttling for best-effort during queue growth; enterprise should see stable p95 even when we shed lower tiers.
- rerank
  - Extremely latency-sensitive; small outputs; should be protected early because it is cheap per request but heavily impacted by queueing.
  - Recommendation: treat as "high priority" within enterprise priority class to keep p95 stable.

Current SLO pain points (what keeps showing up)
1) Mixed workload head-of-line blocking
- Long prompts and batch jobs raise queue depth and scheduler lag; short interactive requests ride the same lane.
- Symptoms: p99 latency spike + timeouts; increased retries; cascading 5xx.

2) Retry storms + ambiguous throttling
- Today: customers see 429 but can’t tell quota vs overload vs global rate limit.
- Result: some clients retry too aggressively; makes bursts worse.

3) Region-specific saturation with slow recovery
- us-east shows faster tail growth under burst because it absorbs overflow and has more multi-tenant mixing.
- Recovery: queue drains slowly; best-effort traffic returns too early and re-triggers pressure.

4) Observability gaps
- We don’t yet have a clean per-route/per-tier shed-rate signal; debugging relies on correlating multiple dashboards.

Proposed MVP protected routes (based on above)
- YES: /v1/chat/completions (incl structured), /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank, /v1/batches (guardrails for isolation).
- Later: /v1/responses (watch growth), legacy /v1/completions (deprecate), audio routes (separate concerns).

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm final list with PM-882: whether /v1/batches is "protected" or "restricted" (different semantics; likely strict admission control with explicit quotas).
- Decide whether we need separate priority class inside enterprise (e.g., Enterprise-P0 for rerank vs Enterprise-P1 for chat) vs keeping one class and handling via per-route budgets.
- Validate ctx-length bucketing feasibility without adding high-cardinality tags (coordinate with Allison/Logan on metrics standard).
- For each protected route: define "safe fallback" policy (if allowed) vs strict shedding only. Early read: rerank should not silently fallback; embeddings may allow region fallback; chat depends on contract.

Change log
- 2026-01-22 (Benji): updated embeddings and rerank peaks after eu-west canary week; added batch route notes.
- 2026-01-09 (Mina/Logan): initial inventory table + tenant notes; aligned route_group names with gateway config draft.
